headline: Bank of America warns of higher interest rates if oil prices continue to rise
summary: Strategists at Bank of America identified a strong correlation between oil prices and interest rates in the U.S., U.K., and Germany, suggesting rates could climb significantly if energy costs remain elevated.
why: Central banks typically raise interest rates to combat inflation caused by rising energy costs, which act as a supply-side shock to the economy.

impacts.name: US 10-year Treasury yield
impacts.why: Higher oil prices increase inflationary pressure, forcing central banks to maintain or raise interest rates.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Rising oil prices increase headline inflation, which historically forces central banks to maintain higher interest rates to stabilize price levels.
